questions.text: Tom is taller than Sam, and Sam is taller than Ali. Who is the shortest?
questions.why: Tom is taller than Sam and Sam is taller than Ali, so Ali is shorter than both.

questions.text: I'm tall when I'm young and short when I'm old. What am I?
questions.why: A candle starts tall and gets shorter as it burns down.

questions.text: Joey has seven sisters. How many children do his parents have?
questions.why: Seven sisters plus Joey himself makes eight.
Each number is a third of the one before: 3 ÷ 3 = 1.

questions.text: In Morse code, S is three dots and O three dashes. How many dots and dashes spell SOS?
A cowboy rides into town on Friday, stays three days and leaves on Friday. How?
questions.why: The day doesn't change at all: his horse is called Friday.

questions.text: How many 4-digit numbers can be made using the digits 1, 2, 3 and 4 once each?
questions.why: There are 4 choices for the first digit, then 3, 2 and 1: 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 = 24.

questions.text: Which common word has three consecutive double letters?
questions.why: BOOKKEEPER has three double letters in a row: bOOKKEEper.

questions.text: Which three different whole numbers give the same answer whether you add them together or multiply them together?
A man pushes his car up to a hotel and tells the owner he is bankrupt. What is he doing?
questions.why: He's playing Monopoly: his token is the car, and he has landed on a hotel he can't afford.

questions.text: Writing numbers out in British English, what is the smallest whole number whose name contains the letter A?
questions.why: Nothing from one to ninety-nine has an A, and neither does 'one hundred'. The first A is the 'and' in 'one hundred AND one'.
